headline: Global shipments of professional service robots rose 24 percent to almost 250,000 units in 2025.
score_reason: Stays at pool 5: an industry-body statistic; a real but broad trend.
importance_line: What changed: robots used by businesses are moving from pilots into daily work in logistics, hotels and cleaning, which matters to workers and to the businesses that buy them; the doubt: these are the industry body's own figures, and it says most humanoid uses still need human control.
summary: The International Federation of Robotics reports, in its World Robotics 2026 Service Robots report, that shipments of professional service robots (robots used by businesses) rose 24 percent in 2025 to almost 250,000 units, with transport and logistics the largest use at 117,500 units. It also says about 7,000 full-size humanoid robots were sold in 2025, and that safety standards, high costs and a weak business case still hold back wider use.
notes: Read in full (press release). Figures are the federation's own.
